title: introduce-reservoir-based-decentralized-scale-synthesizer
author: Aisha Patel
ci_status: pass (initial flaky timing failure; rerun green)
description: Motivation: production fleets see many short-lived microbursts from tenant traffic patterns which cause oscillatory autoscaling and wasted headroom. This PR implements a lightweight reservoir-based "decentralized scale synthesizer" that runs alongside the existing autoscaler to smooth short spikes while preserving throughput guarantees and predictable tail latency. Design summary: 1) each node maintains a small local reservoir credit accounting window that decays over time and is topped up by observed idle capacity; 2) the synthesizer aggregates ephemeral credits across replicas via a gossip-style delta protocol to create a soft, decentralized pool without a central control plane lock; 3) scaling decisions use a two-stage policy: local fast-path uses reservoir credits to accept short bursts without triggering scale-up, while the slow-path falls back to the cluster autoscaler when sustained demand exceeds reservoir thresholds. Key properties: bounded amplification (reservoir caps per-tenant and per-node), graceful decay to avoid persistent overcommit, and deterministic backoff in preemption scenarios. Telemetry and observability: added reservoir inflow/outflow metrics, reservoir_utilization_percentile by tenant, reservoir_credit_evictions, and a debug endpoint to snapshot local reservoir state. Feature flags: env FLAG_RESERVOIR_SYNTHETIC=true enables the synthesizer and FLAG_RESERVOIR_GOSSIP controls gossip interval. Backwards compatibility: autoscaler API unchanged, synthesizer registers as an optional operator. Rollout plan: gated behind feature flags, start with canary on dedicated fleets for low-risk tenants, monitor latency and headroom burn rates for 72 hours, then progressive rollout. Tests: unit tests for credit accounting and gossip reconciliation, integration tests simulating mixed-duration microbursts, and a synthetic benchmark showing 18% reduction in unnecessary scale-ups and 12% lower 99th percentile latency for bursty workloads in our lab. Risk and mitigations: gossip divergence detected in tests fixed by introducing monotonic vector clocks and periodic full-state reconciliation. Migration notes: no live migration required; operators can toggle off to immediately disable accepting reservoir credits. See docs/design/reservoir-synthesizer.md for detailed algorithms and math. Checklist: - [x] design doc - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] telemetry dashboards - [x] canary rollout plan
commits: 1) add reservoir synthesizer core loop and credit accounting; 2) implement gossip delta reconciler and vector clocks; 3) integrate synthesizer with local admission fast-path; 4) add telemetry hooks and dashboards; 5) tests and docs; 6) fix flake in integration test timing
review_comments: Daniel Kim: 'Can you elaborate on how vector clocks prevent split-brain in high churn clusters?' Author: 'Vector clocks are scoped to reservoir deltas and we only accept deltas with monotonically increasing sequence numbers per node; in practice this prevents applying stale negative deltas. We also fallback to full-state reconciliation on mismatch which is in the implementation.' Priya Shah: 'Need a clear knob to stop credit acceptance per-tenant for compliance customers.' Author: 'Added per-tenant opt-out via tenant metadata and feature flag checks in the admission fast-path.' Connor Lee: 'Telemetry looks good but add a gauge for reservoir headroom impact on node memory to catch leaks.' Author: 'Added reservoir_memory_bytes metric and a unit test around memory reset after reconciliation.' After fixes reviewers approved and requested squash merge.
